newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ ACT's Prebble second in Wellington Central poll.
newsitem.headline: NZ ACT's Prebble second in Wellington Central poll.

text.p: The leader of the free-market ACT New Zealand Party has jumped into second place in the race for the Wellington Central seat, a poll on Thursday showed.
ACT leader Richard Prebble polled 24 percent, up three on a similar poll last week according to a poll in the "Evening Post" newspaper.
The ruling National Party's Mark Thomas maintained his lead on 27 pereent, up two, while opposition Labour's Alick Shaw was a close third on 23 percent, down one.

Under the rules of the new proportional representation system adopted by New Zealand, if Prebble wins the seat, ACT, an ally of National, would qualify for seats in Parliament without needing to break the five percent threshold.
Sitting MP Pauline Gardiner of National's coalition partner United New Zealand remained in fourth place with 15 percent support, down four.
A rebel group in National have urged Thomas to stand aside to help Prebble win the seat and secure a coalition partner for National, but he has refused
The poll of 500 voters recorded a narrowing of the gap between National and Labour in the party list vote which determines the overall number of seats a party will get in parliament.
National scored 47 percent, down six, while Labour was on 22 percent, up two.
Labour's likely allies after the October 12 election showed little change with the left wing Alliance down one at 12 percent and economic nationalist New Zealand First steady on six percent.
ACT's party support was up two at six percent and the Christian Coalition was up one at four percent.
Fifteen percent of those polled were undecided.

Some 60 percent said they had a favourable view of Labour leader Helen Clark compared with 56 percent for Prime Minister Jim Bolger, 39 percent for Alliance leader Jim Anderton and 18 percent for New Zealand First leader Winston Peters.
